prompt:
A 72-second instrumental film-score cue of numb grief and shock, not drama, for a small, close chamber group: a muted string group (two cellos, two violas, two violins; con sordino, no vibrato), one solo cello, and a felt-muted upright piano, all recorded close and dry, in tune at A = 440. Key centre A minor, with the B-flat a semitone above as the uneasy note. Very slow, beatless free time. Piano at the start, then pianissimo and softer. Dark and muffled: the top octaves stay empty. The lowest note is the cellos' low C; no double bass.
[0:00 - 0:08] From silence, the low strings bloom softly on a dark A minor chord, blurred and distant; over it the solo cello plays one slow falling phrase of five notes, E, D, C, B-flat, A, about one every 1.2 seconds, plain, unadorned and exhausted, and settles on the A.
[0:08 - 0:26] The strings freeze into one cold, still open fifth, A2 and E3, barely audible, breathing slowly in and out. Nothing moves.
[0:26 - 0:43] The felt piano plays single low notes far apart, about one every five seconds (A, then E, then C, then A), each left to ring and fade, while the open fifth holds quietly underneath. Grey and numb.
[0:43 - 0:55] Everything thins to one sustained A on the muted cellos (A3, the A below middle C), very quiet and still, with no accents at all.
[0:55 - 1:12] A viola joins a semitone above on B-flat (B-flat3), and the two notes hold together, pianissimo, softly grinding, completely static to the very end; do not change, resolve or fade (it will be cut off).
Instrumental only, no vocals, no choir. Avoid: percussion, timpani, pulses, pizzicato, risers, braams, impacts, swells, crescendos, a big sad melody, a swelling romantic string adagio, lush vibrato, trailer clichés, high strings, and anything bright.
